summary: Tennessee Division of Forestry tower 6-1 in Sumner County, listed at 991 ft; the state list marks it removed and no source read gives its build date or site.

facts.status_note: Tennessee's tower list marks it removed.

events.note: Tennessee's 1976 list of towers is the source of the state forest tower numbers; the Westmoreland tower appears on it as 6-1.

evidence.supports: Westmoreland entry: Sumner County, listed at 991 ft, tower number 6-1, removed
Table numbers are state forest tower numbers
evidence.quote: Numbers in the table (e.g., 4-7) are state forest tower numbers

evidence.supports: Numbers come from a 1976 list of towers
The towers formed the state's fire-detection network 1933 to 1975
evidence.quote: fire towers formed the physical manifestation of TDF’s fire detection network between 1933 and 1975

evidence.supports: Exact number and location of 1930s towers is unknown
evidence.quote: the exact quantity and location of the fire towers constructed in the 1930s is unknown

evidence.supports: CCC reported to have built 98 lookout houses and towers in Tennessee during the 1930s (the study's 'this period', which follows its 1930s sentence)
evidence.quote: it is reported that the CCC was responsible for the construction of 98 lookout houses and towers in Tennessee during this period

evidence.supports: Many of the 208 network towers removed or awaiting demolition, from disuse or lease expiry
evidence.quote: Many of the 208 fire lookout towers once part of TDF’s fire detection network have been removed or are awaiting demolition as a result of disuse or the expiration of lease agreements with private property owners

sources.title: Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers, 1933 to 1975 (National Register multiple property documentation)
sources.publisher: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only tower-specific source is one row in the Tennessee landforms list (Sumner County, 991 ft, number 6-1, removed). The NRHP study gives program context only; its 98-tower CCC figure is for the whole state and the 1930s (the study's 'this period') and the story does not attach it to this tower. The story now dates the CCC figure to the 1930s, not 1933-1975, and footnotes the two claims that had none. No build date, height, design, staffing or site description was found in the sources read. The Tennessee Division of Forestry was not searched directly. Two searches and about six page reads used.
